question.problem:
Let $X$ be the outcome of rolling an unfair  six-sided die that follows the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ |
question.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4)+5\cdot f(5)+6\cdot f(6) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+2(\frac{3}{8})+3(\frac{1}{4})+4(\frac{1}{8})+5(\frac{1}{16})+6(\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{45}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{5}^{2}\cdot f(5)+{6}^{2}\cdot f(6) \\  & =1(\frac{1}{8})+4(\frac{3}{8})+9(\frac{1}{4})+16(\frac{1}{8})+25(\frac{1}{16})+36(\frac{1}{16}) \\  & =\frac{155}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{155}{16}-{(\frac{45}{16})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{155}{16}-\frac{2025}{256} \\  & =\frac{455}{256}.\end{aligned}
$$
